challenges.name: leaderboard-projection-quiz
challenges.title: Gaps, sequence numbers and tie order
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the leaderboard projection: a learner's events arriving out of order, and the order Redis gives to two learners with the same score.

questions.question:
Consumer log of the leaderboard projection for one learner (the outbox stamps every event of a learner with learnerSeq 1, 2, 3, ...):

14:20:01.310 recv e_5501 u_an learnerSeq=5 challenge.passed +30   lastApplied=4 -> apply, lastApplied=5
14:20:01.402 recv e_5503 u_an learnerSeq=7 challenge.passed +20   lastApplied=5 -> wait (missing 6)
14:20:01.977 recv e_5502 u_an learnerSeq=6 progress.updated +10   lastApplied=5 -> apply 6, then 7, lastApplied=7

Statement: "If the projection had applied e_5503 as soon as it arrived and set lastApplied=7, it would then have dropped e_5502 as already applied, and u_an's score would be 10 points short."
questions.explanation: True. With a single per-learner high-water mark, "learnerSeq <= lastApplied" is how the projection recognises events it has already applied. Jumping to 7 makes event 6 look old, so the lesson completion (+10) is skipped forever. The points are additive, so the score would be permanently wrong until a rebuild. Holding 7 until 6 arrives keeps the rule simple and correct: apply in sequence, and the high-water mark always means "everything up to here is in". The misconception is that "apply only newer versions" is enough; it is enough when each event carries the whole new state (last write wins), not when events carry deltas.

questions.question:
The projection writes scores to a Redis sorted set:

09:00:12 ZINCRBY lb:all-time 40 u_c
09:05:47 ZINCRBY lb:all-time 40 u_a

redis> ZREVRANGE lb:all-time 0 -1 WITHSCORES
1) "u_c"
2) "40"
3) "u_a"
4) "40"

The product rule says: on equal points, the learner who got there first ranks higher.

Statement: "ZREVRANGE lists u_c before u_a because u_c reached 40 points first, so the sorted set already implements the product's tie rule."
questions.explanation: False. Members with equal scores are ordered by the member string, and ZREVRANGE uses descending lexicographic order: "u_c" > "u_a", so u_c comes first whatever the timing. Swap the two ZINCRBY calls and the output stays the same, which is the quick test that proves it. To implement "first to reach the score wins", encode the tie-breaker into the score (for example points * 10^10 + (10^10 - 1 - sequenceWhenReached)) or sort ties in the application. The misconception is reading a coincidence in one sample as the rule.

challenges.name: leaderboard-projection-from-events
challenges.title: A leaderboard projection from progress events
challenges.description:
Implement ProjectionLeaderboard, the CodeDev leaderboard projection. It consumes events from the event bus (at-least-once delivery, so redeliveries happen, and events of one learner can arrive out of order) and keeps an "all-time" board and one board per week. PostgreSQL stays the source of truth; this projection can always be rebuilt from events.

Events (untrusted JSON): { eventId, type, userId, learnerSeq, week, ... } where type is "challenge.passed" (with points) or "progress.updated" (with lessonPercent and coursePercent). learnerSeq is the learner's own sequence number (1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps, stamped by the outbox). An event is invalid when it is not an object, eventId, userId or week is not a non-empty string, learnerSeq is not an integer >= 1, the type is another string, points is not an integer from 1 to 500 (challenge.passed), or lessonPercent / coursePercent is not an integer from 0 to 100 (progress.updated).

apply(event) returns, checked in this order: "invalid" (ignored, and its eventId is not remembered); "duplicate" when the eventId was already accepted; "stale" when that learner's learnerSeq was already applied or is already waiting (a different event id with a used sequence number); otherwise "accepted". An accepted event is applied when its learnerSeq is the learner's next one (last applied + 1, starting at 1); otherwise it waits. After applying, keep applying that learner's waiting events while the next learnerSeq is there. waiting() returns the number of accepted events not applied yet.

Points when applied: challenge.passed adds points; progress.updated adds 10 when lessonPercent is 100, plus 50 when coursePercent is 100 (so 0, 10, 50 or 60). Points go to the "all-time" board and to the board named by the event's week. An event worth 0 points changes no board, and a learner appears on a board only with more than 0 points there.

top(board, n) and rank(board, userId) use one order per board: more points first; on equal points, the learner whose points on that board changed earlier (in the order events were applied) first. rank is the 1-based position in that order; rank returns null when the learner is not on the board. The runner prints, after each batch, the outcome counts, waiting(), the top N of "all-time" and of the batch's week, and the watched learners. Do not change the types or the test runner.
hints: What should happen to u_an's score when learnerSeq 3 arrives before learnerSeq 2? And when the same eventId arrives a second time an hour later?

Keep per learner: the last applied learnerSeq and a map of waiting events by learnerSeq; globally: the set of accepted eventIds and a counter that goes up each time an event is applied. Each board entry needs the points and the counter value of its last change, which is the tie-breaker.

A similar case with different data: last applied for u_x is 2, waiting is {4}. Event 3 arrives: accept it, apply 3, then 4, last applied becomes 4, waiting is empty. Another event with learnerSeq 4 and a new id is now stale; the same id as event 3 is a duplicate. If u_x and u_y both have 70 points and u_y's last change was applied first, u_y ranks above u_x.
